analogs.covers: Pack and hunting: a loud nomadic pack that drives prey into dead ends and corners
Terrain and solo play: forest-and-cliffside ambusher, able to hunt big prey alone

headline: A dingo pack led by dominant males that herds prey into dead ends, with a cougar's forest-and-cliff ambush.

setting.label: Forests and cliffsides
setting.note: Nomadic; 'primarily travel through forests and cliffsides in search of their next meal'.

playsLike: You are a large, aggressive tyrannosaurid in a pack of up to 6 led by a dominant male or a bonded male pair. Females raise the cubs and defend them fiercely. Hunts are teamwork: one herder flushes prey toward two hidden ambushers, then the party corners it. Solo you take prey up to Large tier, ambush or raid nests; 2+ of you can take Apex. Unless you are alone, you fear no other dinosaur.

why.text: Works together to herd prey into dead ends and corners, with one 'herder' and two ambushers. Dingoes drive prey into fences, water and gullies (official inspiration).
Travels through forests and cliffsides, and a solo animal ambushes its targets. That is cougar country and cougar style (official inspiration).
Dominant males lead hunting, migration and courtship and fight bloody takeover battles; ungrouped males must submit or be chased out.
Packs are loud but go 'dangerously quiet when in pursuit of prey'.
Large tier, 3,500 combat weight, 600 HP, sprint 1,025 held for 91 s.

notLike: Dingo packs revolve around one breeding pair; Daspletosaurus males may court up to four females each.
Cougars are solitary, while Daspletosaurus prefers the pack.
